**Private reasoning:** The ceiling is still null, so my character's withdrawal rule (triggered only by an announced ceiling ≥ 8) does not apply — I stay and bid normally. This lot is worth 10 plus a 3-coin commission, giving an effective value of 13 to me. My bank of 6 caps my bid, but every bid up to 6 is strongly profitable (winning at 6 nets +7). Since a higher bid weakly increases my win probability and all affordable bids are profitable, bidding my maximum (6) is optimal — it's the only way to beat a rival bidding in the 5-6 range (ties favor rivals, so 6 only loses to a 6+ bid, which I couldn't contest anyway). Winning this big lot is also nearly essential to closing the score gap with Bidder 2 (11 vs 20) for the 5-coin finder's fee, and if a high ceiling is announced in later rounds I'd be withdrawing anyway, making current profitable spending even more attractive. If I win, my bank becomes 6 − 6 + 3 = 3; if I lose, it stays 6 — no downside relative to shading.
